answer: An agent marketplace allocates bidding power in proportion to tokens locked in escrow for 30 days, not the number of accounts. Whether bidding to reserve a wharf, plan a voyage, or write a sonnet, an agent must supply that collateral. Splitting 100 tokens across a thousand identities yields no more total bidding power than staking them under one name. To gain influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, paying financing and opportunity costs.
